title: Proof-pull an anchor plate to its test load while holding the plate
instruction: Proof-test the grey anchor plate: pull its yellow handle until the gauge carriage reaches the green band, hold it for one second, then let it ease back, without the plate sliding.
context: Temporary roof anchors are proof-loaded before a worker clips on: the tester pulls to a target load while pinning the base (O*NET 47-2181, 47-2211, 47-4099). An untested anchor can fail under a fall.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Grey plate 12 (x) x 30 (y) x 1.5 cm, 0.8 kg, friction 0.1, centre x 30, y -2, with an orange fin (7 x 2 x 4 cm) at its far left end (y 10). A yellow carriage (5 cm long) on a rail along y, with a yellow handle 4 x 2 x 4 cm tall at x 30, y -13, is pulled back by a spring of 80 N/m (about 4.4-5.6 N at the band); stroke 9 cm, pulled toward the left. A scale beside the rail has a green band at 5.5-7.0 cm of travel and a red zone at 8-9 cm.
scoring: Read at the end from the carriage travel and the plate position. 0 if the carriage ever passes 8 cm, or the plate moves more than 1.5 cm, lifts more than 1 cm or tilts more than 20 degrees (after the first 2 s). 0.25 if the carriage was pulled 2 cm; 0.5 if it reached the band (5.5 cm); 0.75 if it stayed inside 5.5-7.0 cm for 1 s with the plate moved at most 5 mm; 1.0 if also it returned to 1 cm or less within 3 s of leaving the band, the plate moved at most 5 mm, and the carriage is still.
reset_notes: Let the carriage return to rest and put the plate back on its marks.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; the gauge reading is the travel of a spring-loaded slider (80 N/m, a modelled spring), not a physical force sensor. The plate is a rigid slab with friction 0.1. Scoring is computed from measured poses and the slider position; nothing is code-driven.
